While both companies stand to benefit from AI, their investment cases do not depend entirely on the technology succeeding. Berkshire first started investing in Apple in 2016, long before generative AI became Wall Street's favorite investment theme. At the time, Buffett recognized something most investors were discounting: Apple wasn't simply a hardware manufacturer. The company had acquired an extremely loyal customer base, possessed a powerful brand, and built a product ecosystem that kept customers sticky. That combination creates what Buffett calls an economic moat , a durable competitive advantage that helps a company protect its profits. Nearly a decade later, Apple's business remains remarkably resilient. Instead of creating a new product every few years, Apple has found different ways to monetize its platform. For example, the company's Services segment includes the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, AppleCare, and other offerings that generate recurring revenue from Apple's installed base of billions of devices worldwide. This is highly attractive because Apple's customers do not need to purchase a new iPhone every year for the company to generate incremental revenue. What makes Apple so different from other speculative AI investments is that the company doesn't really need AI to become its largest revenue source. Sure, AI can strengthen Apple's products and encourage customers to upgrade. But the company's established hardware business, expanding services ecosystem, and powerful brand already support substantial earnings and cash flow. Moreover, Apple also consistently returns capital to shareholders through stock buybacks and dividends, another characteristic Buffett appreciates. Although Berkshire has reduced its Apple position over time, the stock remains its largest holding. That continued exposure underscores the enduring appeal of Apple stock. Berkshire first disclosed a position in Alphabet in November 2025 and has since added to it over the past year. The company owns two of the world's most recognizable brands, Google and YouTube, both of which boast highly profitable advertising businesses. AI simply enhances their capabilities, but Alphabet doesn't need to build an entirely new platform to justify its long-term potential. The biggest risk facing AI investors isn't that the technology fails. It's that investors overestimate how much money individual companies will make from it. History is filled with examples of promising technologies that transformed society without generating attractive returns for each company involved. This is what makes Apple and Alphabet compelling. Both companies have diversified business models , recognizable brands, significant competitive advantages, and established sources of recurring cash flow. They also have the financial flexibility to invest in AI without depending entirely on that infrastructure for their survival. For investors seeking AI stocks to buy and hold forever, I see Apple and Alphabet as prime examples. Their existing businesses already generate attractive growth, while AI merely offers an additional tailwind. That combination resembles the kind of long-term investment Buffett has favored throughout his legendary career. While both companies stand to benefit from AI, their investment cases do not depend entirely on the technology succeeding. Berkshire first started investing in Apple in 2016, long before generative AI became Wall Street's favorite investment theme. The company had acquired an extremely loyal customer base, possessed a powerful brand, and built a product ecosystem that kept customers sticky. That combination creates what Buffett calls an economic moat , a durable competitive advantage that helps a company protect its profits. Nearly a decade later, Apple's business remains remarkably resilient. Instead of creating a new product every few years, Apple has found different ways to monetize its platform. For example, the company's Services segment includes the App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, AppleCare, and other offerings that generate recurring revenue from Apple's installed base of billions of devices worldwide. This is highly attractive because Apple's customers do not need to purchase a new iPhone every year for the company to generate incremental revenue. What makes Apple so different from other speculative AI investments is that the company doesn't really need AI to become its largest revenue source. Sure, AI can strengthen Apple's products and encourage customers to upgrade. But the company's established hardware business, expanding services ecosystem, and powerful brand already support substantial earnings and cash flow. Moreover, Apple also consistently returns capital to shareholders through stock buybacks and dividends, another characteristic Buffett appreciates. Although Berkshire has reduced its Apple position over time, the stock remains its largest holding. That continued exposure underscores the enduring appeal of Apple stock. Berkshire first disclosed a position in Alphabet in November 2025 and has since added to it over the past year. Like Apple, Alphabet has many characteristics associated with Buffett's investment philosophy . The company owns two of the world's most recognizable brands, Google and YouTube, both of which boast highly profitable advertising businesses. AI simply enhances their capabilities, but Alphabet doesn't need to build an entirely new platform to justify its long-term potential. The biggest risk facing AI investors isn't that the technology fails. It's that investors overestimate how much money individual companies will make from it. History is filled with examples of promising technologies that transformed society without generating attractive returns for each company involved. This is what makes Apple and Alphabet compelling. Both companies have diversified business models , recognizable brands, significant competitive advantages, and established sources of recurring cash flow. They also have the financial flexibility to invest in AI without depending entirely on that infrastructure for their survival. For investors seeking AI stocks to buy and hold forever, I see Apple and Alphabet as prime examples. If you hold Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) and Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) and you want to experience even more volatility and risk than you already do, you're in luck. On Oct. 2, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved an exchange to list Volatility Shares' 3x Bitcoin ETF and the 3x Ether ETF, both of which are leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that aim to offer exposure to triple the daily price action of those two coins. Neither fund is available to trade yet, since a separate SEC registration step required before launch hasn't been scheduled (as I write this on Oct. 21). But will either of these ETFs be worth buying after they start trading? Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Both of the proposed ETFs hold futures , contracts to buy an asset at a set price on a later date, and reset their exposure every day. That reset is necessary for the constant leverage provided by the ETFs to work, but it's also the source of a dangerous trap for investors. If a coin rises 10% in a day, the fund rises about 30% that day. This is the part that everyone gets excited about. The problem is that if the coin's price then proceeds to fall back to where it started, which is to say a drop of about 9.1% that would leave a spot holder with a gain of $0, the leveraged ETF shareholder ends up with losses of about 5.5% instead. This very example can be found verbatim in the Volatility Shares prospectus for the fund. It's also the same drag that recently hit another very similar leveraged Bitcoin ETF, the Volatility Shares 2x Bitcoin ETF. It lost 61.9% in the 12-month period ending on Oct. 21 despite Bitcoin falling only 25.1% in the same period. The prospectus indicates that the Bitcoin fund will charge a 1.85% management fee per year, and it estimates that the Bitcoin and Ether funds must earn 1.98% and 2.78% a year just to break even. What's more, while steady returns could well accumulate into a big paper gain, the leverage math means that it often only takes one rough down day to erase significant value. These ETFs are not really intended for average investors to buy and then hold for long periods of time. They're for hedge funds and institutional investors making complex trades with multiple assets and hedges. However, both coins are still worth buying for patient investors. Buying Ethereum or Bitcoin directly, or via spot ETFs, is a much better move than any leveraged play, as it costs far less in terms of fees, and they're also not capable of experiencing leverage-induced downside volatility. passages: On October 2, 2026, the SEC officially approved the first 3x Bitcoin ETF in the United States, allowing Volatility Shares to list triple-leveraged funds for Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) and Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) on Cboe BZX.
This approval also includes 3x funds associated with gold, silver, crude oil, and natural gas.
Both Bitcoin and Ether can be quite volatile, which can accelerate a leveraged fund's decay.
For instance, Bitcoin traded between $80,837 and $87,397 on September 21, an 8% range in a single day.
The proposed 3x Bitcoin fund, ticker BITH, and the 3x Ether fund, ticker ETHK, will rely on futures contracts rather than holding the physical coins.
Volatility Shares has experience offering leveraged crypto funds, including its existing 2x Bitcoin fund, BITX, so these new products build on its established expertise.
The daily reset feature introduces volatility decay, the primary risk associated with these funds.
For example, if Bitcoin increases by 10% one day but then decreases by 10% the next, Bitcoin would end up down 1%.
However, a 3x fund could show a 30% gain followed by a 30% loss, leading to an overall decline of 9%.
Since early August, Bitcoin has gained roughly 32% over 60 days, yet it remains about 2% below its 2026 starting point.
As of October 5, Bitcoin was trading around $86,189, down 30% over the past year, while Ether was around $2,724, down 39% and 45% off its peak.
Volatility decay means a 10% Bitcoin gain then 10% loss produces a 9% fund loss versus just 1% for Bitcoin directly.
For those looking to capitalize on a potential multi-month rebound, it's often better to hold the actual coins or invest in an unleveraged spot fund, which doesn't have the same reset challenges.
The situation may change if the final fund specifics indicate a longer investment horizon or if Bitcoin stabilizes with consistent price movements.
Both funds will rebalance at the end of each trading day, resetting their exposure to three times the remaining balance.

For those looking to capitalize on a potential multi-month rebound, it's often better to hold the actual coins or invest in an unleveraged spot fund, which doesn't have the same reset challenges. The situation may change if the final fund specifics indicate a longer investment horizon or if Bitcoin stabilizes with consistent price movements. Until then, a 3x Bitcoin ETF may appeal only to short-term traders.

extraction.body: If you hold Bitcoin ( BTC -0.33% ) and Ethereum ( ETH -1.64% ) and you want to experience even more volatility and risk than you already do, you're in luck. On Oct. 2, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved an exchange to list Volatility Shares' 3x Bitcoin ETF and the 3x Ether ETF, both of which are leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that aim to offer exposure to triple the daily price action of those two coins. Neither fund is available to trade yet, since a separate SEC registration step required before launch hasn't been scheduled (as I write this on Oct. 21). But will either of these ETFs be worth buying after they start trading? Both of the proposed ETFs hold futures , contracts to buy an asset at a set price on a later date, and reset their exposure every day. That reset is necessary for the constant leverage provided by the ETFs to work, but it's also the source of a dangerous trap for investors. If a coin rises 10% in a day, the fund rises about 30% that day. This is the part that everyone gets excited about. The problem is that if the coin's price then proceeds to fall back to where it started, which is to say a drop of about 9.1% that would leave a spot holder with a gain of $0, the leveraged ETF shareholder ends up with losses of about 5.5% instead. This very example can be found verbatim in the Volatility Shares prospectus for the fund. It's also the same drag that recently hit another very similar leveraged Bitcoin ETF, the Volatility Shares 2x Bitcoin ETF. It lost 61.9% in the 12-month period ending on Oct. 21 despite Bitcoin falling only 25.1% in the same period. The prospectus indicates that the Bitcoin fund will charge a 1.85% management fee per year, and it estimates that the Bitcoin and Ether funds must earn 1.98% and 2.78% a year just to break even. What's more, while steady returns could well accumulate into a big paper gain, the leverage math means that it often only takes one rough down day to erase significant value. These ETFs are not really intended for average investors to buy and then hold for long periods of time. They're for hedge funds and institutional investors making complex trades with multiple assets and hedges. However, both coins are still worth buying for patient investors. Buying Ethereum or Bitcoin directly, or via spot ETFs, is a much better move than any leveraged play, as it costs far less in terms of fees, and they're also not capable of experiencing leverage-induced downside volatility. And that means you'll be able to hold them for years -- and hopefully, get a good return along the way instead of getting liquidated. Alex Carchidi has positions in Bitcoin and Ethereum. sources.title: The SEC Approves the First 3x Bitcoin and Ether Funds: Understanding the Risks Involved - AOL.com
passages: On October 2, 2026, the SEC officially approved the first 3x Bitcoin ETF in the United States, allowing Volatility Shares to list triple-leveraged funds for Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) and Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) on Cboe BZX.
This approval also includes 3x funds associated with gold, silver, crude oil, and natural gas.
Both Bitcoin and Ether can be quite volatile, which can accelerate a leveraged fund's decay.
For instance, Bitcoin traded between $80,837 and $87,397 on September 21, an 8% range in a single day.
The proposed 3x Bitcoin fund, ticker BITH, and the 3x Ether fund, ticker ETHK, will rely on futures contracts rather than holding the physical coins.
Volatility Shares has experience offering leveraged crypto funds, including its existing 2x Bitcoin fund, BITX, so these new products build on its established expertise.
The daily reset feature introduces volatility decay, the primary risk associated with these funds.
For example, if Bitcoin increases by 10% one day but then decreases by 10% the next, Bitcoin would end up down 1%.
However, a 3x fund could show a 30% gain followed by a 30% loss, leading to an overall decline of 9%.
Since early August, Bitcoin has gained roughly 32% over 60 days, yet it remains about 2% below its 2026 starting point.
As of October 5, Bitcoin was trading around $86,189, down 30% over the past year, while Ether was around $2,724, down 39% and 45% off its peak.
Volatility decay means a 10% Bitcoin gain then 10% loss produces a 9% fund loss versus just 1% for Bitcoin directly.
For those looking to capitalize on a potential multi-month rebound, it's often better to hold the actual coins or invest in an unleveraged spot fund, which doesn't have the same reset challenges.
The situation may change if the final fund specifics indicate a longer investment horizon or if Bitcoin stabilizes with consistent price movements.
Both funds will rebalance at the end of each trading day, resetting their exposure to three times the remaining balance.

On Oct. 2, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved an exchange to list Volatility Shares' 3x Bitcoin ETF and the 3x Ether ETF, both of which are leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that aim to offer exposure to triple the daily price action of those two coins.

Neither fund is available to trade yet, since a separate SEC registration step required before launch hasn't been scheduled (as I write this on Oct. 21). But will either of these ETFs be worth buying after they start trading?

Both of the proposed ETFs hold futures , contracts to buy an asset at a set price on a later date, and reset their exposure every day. That reset is necessary for the constant leverage provided by the ETFs to work, but it's also the source of a dangerous trap for investors.
If a coin rises 10% in a day, the fund rises about 30% that day. This is the part that everyone gets excited about.

The problem is that if the coin's price then proceeds to fall back to where it started, which is to say a drop of about 9.1% that would leave a spot holder with a gain of $0, the leveraged ETF shareholder ends up with losses of about 5.5% instead. This very example can be found verbatim in the Volatility Shares prospectus for the fund. It's also the same drag that recently hit another very similar leveraged Bitcoin ETF, the Volatility Shares 2x Bitcoin ETF.
It lost 61.9% in the 12-month period ending on Oct. 21 despite Bitcoin falling only 25.1% in the same period.

extraction.body: 31: Additional victims have been identified by the Tempe Police Department following an investigation into a district employee accused of misusing and downloading videos of students in “various states of undress,” according to Tempe Union High School District. The Tempe Union High School District Superintendent wrote: A former Tempe Union High School employee was arrested and booked into Tempe City Jail following an investigation into apparent inappropriate use and download of security video footage, according to the Tempe Police Department. Authorities say they were notified by a security supervisor alleging the footage was being misused after an audit of 28-year-old Antony Cruz's video activity. Investigators are trying to determine the scope of the activity and any potential victims who were impacted.Tempe Police said Cruz was arrested on seven counts of voyeurism. He has since been terminated from District employment. ABC15 has been told Cruz, who was a surveillance officer with the district, was not housed at Corona del Sol High School, where the alleged crime occurred. The room referenced in the investigation is a dance room at the school. It is not a locker room and was never designated by the District or school administration as a changing area. The security camera in the dance room was installed in 2024 for campus safety and security purposes related to the room’s exterior access.The Tempe High School District has begun an internal investigation to determine how and why that occurred, whether established procedures were followed, the room's usage, and what corrective actions may be necessary.Court documents said Cruz gained access to the camera that had "inadvertently been left functioning," and allegedly downloaded videos to his personal devices. Police records say the videos included female students in "various states of undress."The police report said Cruz admitted to attempting sexual acts while viewing them, but Cruz denied that specific allegation in court over the weekend. "I did not have any sexual stimulation or sexual anything with the videos. I saved it for documentation purposes," he said, also telling the court he tried to move the cameras and notify his superiors about them. He told the judge during his court appearance that he "felt uncomfortable" with the cameras and that he was "getting denied every single time" he asked to get rid of them.The district security supervisor notified Tempe Police on Friday after discovering the misuse during an audit. This remains an ongoing investigation and we are working closely with Tempe PD in regards to when details can be shared with our families.As soon as we are able to share additional information without jeopardizing the investigation, we will contact you immediately.Dr. Stacia WilsonSuperintendent, Tempe Union High School DistrictDear Corona del Sol Families,As you know from my prior message, yesterday we were notified that a Tempe Union employee was detained and questioned by Tempe PD. extraction.body: 31: Additional victims have been identified by the Tempe Police Department following an investigation into a district employee accused of misusing and downloading videos of students in “various states of undress,” according to Tempe Union High School District. The Tempe Union High School District Superintendent wrote: A former Tempe Union High School employee was arrested and booked into Tempe City Jail following an investigation into apparent inappropriate use and download of security video footage, according to the Tempe Police Department. Authorities say they were notified by a security supervisor alleging the footage was being misused after an audit of 28-year-old Antony Cruz's video activity. Investigators are trying to determine the scope of the activity and any potential victims who were impacted.Tempe Police said Cruz was arrested on seven counts of voyeurism. He has since been terminated from District employment. ABC15 has been told Cruz, who was a surveillance officer with the district, was not housed at Corona del Sol High School, where the alleged crime occurred. The room referenced in the investigation is a dance room at the school. It is not a locker room and was never designated by the District or school administration as a changing area. The security camera in the dance room was installed in 2024 for campus safety and security purposes related to the room’s exterior access.The Tempe High School District has begun an internal investigation to determine how and why that occurred, whether established procedures were followed, the room's usage, and what corrective actions may be necessary.Court documents said Cruz gained access to the camera that had "inadvertently been left functioning," and allegedly downloaded videos to his personal devices. Police records say the videos included female students in "various states of undress."The police report said Cruz admitted to attempting sexual acts while viewing them, but Cruz denied that specific allegation in court over the weekend. "I did not have any sexual stimulation or sexual anything with the videos. I saved it for documentation purposes," he said, also telling the court he tried to move the cameras and notify his superiors about them. He told the judge during his court appearance that he "felt uncomfortable" with the cameras and that he was "getting denied every single time" he asked to get rid of them.The district security supervisor notified Tempe Police on Friday after discovering the misuse during an audit. Cruz was arrested Saturday, but court documents say the videos were accessed and downloaded in July. "There should be more changes, maybe do more auditing," said Justine, a parent of a Corona del Sol High student.While the district superintendent acknowledged the distressing situation in an email to families below, when ABC15 asked the district about why the camera was still active when it should've been disabled, and if he accessed those cameras from the school or district office, they didn't comment, citing the ongoing investigation.However, the district did say there are currently no cameras in any areas designated as changing areas, bathrooms, or classrooms. ABC15 also asked the district where this temporary locker room was located, but a spokesperson said they couldn't comment due to the investigation. You send your kids to school; on top of safety and violence, we're worried about predators and stuff out there, too," Justine said.The district said all district employees do undergo background checks. Stacia Wilson sent the following statements out to district families:Dear Tempe Union Families,Earlier today, we were notified that a Tempe Union employee, Antony Cruz, was detained and taken into custody by Tempe PD. He had been placed on administrative leave prior to the workday beginning on Friday, August 21.We want to be transparent and share this news with our TUHSD community so you hear it from us first. We anticipate that you may see or hear media coverage of this incident. Additional details are below for Tempe PD’s press release.Please rest assured that the safety of our students is always our first priority. This remains an ongoing investigation and we are working closely with Tempe PD in regards to when details can be shared with our families.As soon as we are able to share additional information without jeopardizing the investigation, we will contact you immediately.Dr. Stacia WilsonSuperintendent, Tempe Union High School DistrictDear Corona del Sol Families,As you know from my prior message, yesterday we were notified that a Tempe Union employee was detained and questioned by Tempe PD. This employee has now been booked on seven counts of voyeurism. We want to be as transparent as we are allowed to be without disrupting Tempe PD’s investigation.We are now able to share with you that the incidents leading to these charges affected Corona del Sol. As of right now, we believe that the inappropriate usage of security footage was isolated to one camera on campus.We are working closely and in full cooperation with Tempe PD as they continue to investigate and identify victims. Tempe PD detectives will be on campus tomorrow to work with administration to identify the victims. Once victims have been identified, Tempe PD will reach out directly to affected families to begin the interview process.Our school and District crisis teams will be in place tomorrow to provide support and resources to affected students.The investigation remains ongoing. Stacia WilsonSuperintendent, Tempe Union High School DistrictThe investigation is ongoing. ABC15 will continue updating this article with the latest information.

extraction.body: Wealthy bitcoin $BTC $84,459.46 holders are increasingly treating their cryptocurrency as an asset to borrow against and generate income from, marking a shift from speculation toward private banking, according to Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca. At the Gibraltar-based bank, customers are seeking cash without selling their bitcoin, putting some of their holdings into income-generating investments, or accumulating more $BTC through interest paid on dollar savings, he said. “Customers are looking for yield and alpha,” Rocca told CoinDesk in an interview, pointing to demand from funds and family offices for accumulation and income products. The behavior reflects bitcoin’s growing maturity, he said. Five or six years ago, the cryptocurrency was primarily viewed as a trading and speculative asset. Today, more holders want financial services built around their existing wealth. Xapo grew out of a bitcoin custody business known for its Swiss bunker storage. Its customers include early adopters who have experienced several halvings (the periodic reductions in new bitcoin issuance), and the rallies and downturns surrounding them. The bank charges an annual membership fee of $1,000, combining dollar banking with access to bitcoin custody, investments and borrowing. Experience has pushed those customers in different directions. Some of the earliest adopters became more willing to take profits as bitcoin reached record prices, having watched gains disappear in previous downturns, Rocca said. Others, including investors who entered around 2018 and 2019, remain determined to hold and prefer borrowing against their coins when they need liquidity. For the profit-takers, selling does not necessarily mean abandoning bitcoin. Some keep the proceeds in dollar savings accounts and receive interest in $BTC , gradually rebuilding their cryptocurrency holdings while retaining cash. Rocca said about 45% of Xapo customers use that feature. Xapo currently advertises a variable base rate of 4.1% on dollar savings, paid in bitcoin, alongside a temporary 4.6% introductory rate for eligible new members. It’s a separate bitcoin credit fund that targets annual returns of up to 4% through lending, exposing investors to credit and counterparty risk. The common thread is the demand to make existing wealth productive. “The theme of this cycle is yield, accumulation, income generation,” Rocca said. Borrowing allows customers to retain exposure to future bitcoin gains, although they also remain exposed to price declines while taking on debt. Traditional banks increasingly acknowledge that clients want bitcoin exposure, Rocca said. Their interest in custody and investment products represents a substantial change from the skepticism he encountered when he began working in crypto in 2016.

sources.title: Crypto Banking Shift: Bitcoin Holders Turn to Yield & Loans - OneSafe.io
passages: The crypto banking landscape is entering a new phase.

On October 24, 2026, Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca told CoinDesk that wealthy bitcoin holders are increasingly seeking loans and yield, treating their cryptocurrency as a collateral asset rather than a speculative instrument ( Cryptonews.net ).

That shift from trading mentality to private‑banking‑style wealth preservation carries immediate consequences for Web3 startups and DAOs that hold bitcoin on their balance sheets, and for the platforms that serve them.

A Web3 startup that raised funds in stablecoins and wants to allocate a portion to bitcoin, or a DAO whose treasury holds ETH and BTC, must now answer the same question the wealthy individual does: how do we extract working capital without undermining our long‑position?
The gap between what wealthy holders can do at a private bank and what a DAO can do with its own treasury is exactly where the next generation of crypto‑banking must deliver.
Bitcoin is being reclassified – from a speculative asset to the foundation of a private‑banking relationship.
Xapo, which began as a custody service, now charges a $1,000 annual membership for a bundle that includes dollar banking, bitcoin custody, investments, and borrowing.
The bank’s clients want the tools previously reserved for traditional wealth management, only anchored to their crypto holdings.
This infrastructure does not provide loans or yield itself; it is the rails that make those strategies executable.
That is the fiat‑crypto integration that wealthy individuals demand from their private bank, packaged for the Web3 business.

Beyond plain bitcoin loans, watch for on‑chain credit markets that use reputation and cash‑flow history, tokenized private credit, and yield‑bearing stablecoins that pay interest directly in the wallet.

For a DAO that already manages its treasury through a platform like OneSafe, adding a yield component may be as simple as allocating a percentage of USDC to a regulated yield protocol and then settling gains back into the fiat account automatically.

However, tapping into yield or borrowing requires an operational layer that securely holds your crypto, connects to lending protocols or banks without manual sweeps, and keeps fiat‑crypto flows transparent for accounting and compliance.
Whether or not your business pursues loans, the market expectation is now that a modern treasury can seamlessly convert crypto to working capital when needed.
For years, companies juggled a traditional bank account for fiat and a separate crypto exchange or custodian.
Only after this operational layer is solid should you explore lending partnerships, so that bitcoin‑backed loans flow directly into a governed fiat account without bottlenecks.
OneSafe brings together your crypto and banking needs in one simple, powerful platform.
Standard Chartered may merge Zodia Custody into its banking division, reshaping crypto banking for businesses and DAOs.

Today, a small but growing group of platforms offers neo‑banking for startups – real multi‑currency accounts, ACH and wire transfers, corporate cards, invoicing, and integrated crypto‑to‑fiat conversions.
Visa’s analysis of crypto in banking confirms that embedded crypto capabilities are rapidly becoming a customer expectation.
As the line between crypto and traditional banking blurs, businesses that have already unified their fiat‑crypto operations will be best positioned to adopt new products without retrofitting.

In another signal of the growing fiat‑crypto integration, September 2026 saw the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issue guidance confirming that national banks can hold stablecoin reserves, a step that makes on‑ramps and off‑ramps more predictable for businesses ( OCC stablecoin rules ). For years, companies juggled a traditional bank account for fiat and a separate crypto exchange or custodian. That fragmentation made it slow and expensive to move value between the two worlds, and near‑impossible to borrow against crypto without manually aggregating balances. As the desire to use bitcoin as collateral spreads, the market is insisting on a unified financial platform that handles both sides natively. Crypto‑friendly business accounts that combine multi‑currency fiat ledgers with secure custody are becoming table stakes. Research from The Financial Brand highlights that cryptocurrency banking is no longer a niche – it’s an operational necessity for modern treasuries. A Web3 startup that raised funds in stablecoins and wants to allocate a portion to bitcoin, or a DAO whose treasury holds ETH and BTC, must now answer the same question the wealthy individual does: how do we extract working capital without undermining our long‑position? Without a flexible, automated treasury stack, they either over‑liquidate or let valuable assets sit idle. The gap between what wealthy holders can do at a private bank and what a DAO can do with its own treasury is exactly where the next generation of crypto‑banking must deliver. The first crypto “banks” were custodial wallets. Over time, exchanges added rudimentary fiat on‑ and off‑ramps, and fintechs began issuing crypto‑backed debit cards. Today, a small but growing group of platforms offers neo‑banking for startups – real multi‑currency accounts, ACH and wire transfers, corporate cards, invoicing, and integrated crypto‑to‑fiat conversions. Visa’s analysis of crypto in banking confirms that embedded crypto capabilities are rapidly becoming a customer expectation. The old workflow – a business bank account at a traditional institution, hardware wallets, and multi‑step manual sell‑withdraw‑transfer cycles – routinely took days and created reconciliation headaches. Legacy banks’ suspicion of cryptocurrency often derailed the process entirely. A growing body of analysis, such as Wolf & Co’s review of how cryptocurrencies may impact the banking industry , underlines the pressure on banks to adapt. Those structural frictions pushed many firms to seek a single infrastructure that could serve as the backbone for both worlds – a crypto‑friendly business account with compliance baked in. However, tapping into yield or borrowing requires an operational layer that securely holds your crypto, connects to lending protocols or banks without manual sweeps, and keeps fiat‑crypto flows transparent for accounting and compliance. Whether or not your business pursues loans, the market expectation is now that a modern treasury can seamlessly convert crypto to working capital when needed. Platforms that offer instant crypto‑to‑fiat conversion give you that agility without a fire sale of your core position. A unified platform replaces the patchwork of bank accounts, exchanges, and custody providers with a single, secure interface. It enables real‑time fiat‑crypto conversion so that funds are available for payroll or vendor payments minutes after a treasury decision, multi‑currency accounts that hold USD, Euro, CAD, and stablecoins side by side, corporate cards with spend limits that can be topped up in crypto, automated bill pay and invoicing in both fiat and stablecoins, and audit trails that satisfy both traditional accountants and on‑chain analysts. This infrastructure does not provide loans or yield itself; it is the rails that make those strategies executable. A startup can borrow against its bitcoin with a third‑party lender, receive the loan in USDC, convert it to fiat on the platform, and pay rent – all within a single, governed environment. That is the fiat‑crypto integration that wealthy individuals demand from their private bank, packaged for the Web3 business. Start with a clear treasury policy that separates operational working capital from strategic holdings. Obtain a crypto‑friendly business account that supports the fiat currencies you need and provides institutional‑grade custody – ideally through a qualified custodian like Fireblocks. Set up automated conversion rules so that a predetermined portion of incoming stablecoin or BTC is converted to fiat for expenses. For DAOs, implement role‑based permissions and multi‑sig workflows that prevent any single contributor from moving funds, while still enabling prompt bill payments. Only after this operational layer is solid should you explore lending partnerships, so that bitcoin‑backed loans flow directly into a governed fiat account without bottlenecks. The following checklist distills criteria that match the current maturity of bitcoin wealth management. Use it to evaluate platforms before you commit. OneSafe, a neo‑banking platform built for global businesses, Web3 startups, and DAOs, illustrates how the pieces fit together. It combines multi‑currency fiat accounts (USD, Euro, CAD, more to come) with secure crypto custody via Fireblocks, instant crypto‑to‑fiat conversion, corporate cards that can be topped up in eight‑plus tokens, and DAO‑specific governance tools. Onboarding is digital and typically completes within a week, and fee schedules are transparent – for example, wire withdrawals cost $25, domestic wires $10, and USDC deposits and withdrawals are free. By handling fiat payments, invoicing, and automated reimbursement workflows alongside crypto, it removes the fragmentation that has historically made it difficult for a startup or DAO to treat its bitcoin treasury as a productive asset. This is not a pitch to replace a lender, but a demonstration of how a unified platform closes the gap between ambition and execution. Regulatory clarity continues to advance. The U.S. OCC guidance on stablecoins (mentioned earlier) and Europe’s MiCA license for stablecoin issuer Qivalis signal growing acceptance of regulated on‑chain value transfer. Meanwhile, the Bank of Israel’s sanctions‑related warning reminds us that integration with the legacy system will always carry compliance obligations. As the line between crypto and traditional banking blurs, businesses that have already unified their fiat‑crypto operations will be best positioned to adopt new products without retrofitting. Beyond plain bitcoin loans, watch for on‑chain credit markets that use reputation and cash‑flow history, tokenized private credit, and yield‑bearing stablecoins that pay interest directly in the wallet. The firms that can plug these products into a fiat‑operational layer will have a first‑mover advantage. For a DAO that already manages its treasury through a platform like OneSafe, adding a yield component may be as simple as allocating a percentage of USDC to a regulated yield protocol and then settling gains back into the fiat account automatically. extraction.body: Wealthy bitcoin BTC $84,459.46 holders are increasingly treating their cryptocurrency as an asset to borrow against and generate income from, marking a shift from speculation toward private banking, according to Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca. At the Gibraltar-based bank, customers are seeking cash without selling their bitcoin, putting some of their holdings into income-generating investments, or accumulating more BTC through interest paid on dollar savings, he said. “Customers are looking for yield and alpha,” Rocca told CoinDesk in an interview, pointing to demand from funds and family offices for accumulation and income products. The behavior reflects bitcoin’s growing maturity, he said. Five or six years ago, the cryptocurrency was primarily viewed as a trading and speculative asset. Today, more holders want financial services built around their existing wealth. Xapo grew out of a bitcoin custody business known for its Swiss bunker storage. Its customers include early adopters who have experienced several halvings (the periodic reductions in new bitcoin issuance), and the rallies and downturns surrounding them. The bank charges an annual membership fee of $1,000, combining dollar banking with access to bitcoin custody, investments and borrowing. Experience has pushed those customers in different directions. Some of the earliest adopters became more willing to take profits as bitcoin reached record prices, having watched gains disappear in previous downturns, Rocca said. Others, including investors who entered around 2018 and 2019, remain determined to hold and prefer borrowing against their coins when they need liquidity. For the profit-takers, selling does not necessarily mean abandoning bitcoin. Some keep the proceeds in dollar savings accounts and receive interest in BTC, gradually rebuilding their cryptocurrency holdings while retaining cash. Rocca said about 45% of Xapo customers use that feature. Xapo currently advertises a variable base rate of 4.1% on dollar savings, paid in bitcoin, alongside a temporary 4.6% introductory rate for eligible new members. It’s a separate bitcoin credit fund that targets annual returns of up to 4% through lending, exposing investors to credit and counterparty risk. The common thread is the demand to make existing wealth productive. “The theme of this cycle is yield, accumulation, income generation,” Rocca said. Borrowing allows customers to retain exposure to future bitcoin gains, although they also remain exposed to price declines while taking on debt. Traditional banks increasingly acknowledge that clients want bitcoin exposure, Rocca said. Their interest in custody and investment products represents a substantial change from the skepticism he encountered when he began working in crypto in 2016. “Big banks are slow,” he said, describing institutions where new products require committee approvals and employees are reluctant to champion activities perceived as risky. Political and regulatory uncertainty adds to that caution. Banks that previously feared repercussions from serving crypto businesses need confidence that a more accommodating environment will endure before committing resources, he said. For now, some institutions are doing enough to meet customer demand through investment products, while stopping short of services that let clients borrow against or directly manage bitcoin wealth. “Them being slow is a good opportunity for firms like Xapo Bank,” Rocca said. He also sees benefits in a measured approach, arguing that another failure involving poorly managed crypto businesses could damage confidence in bitcoin itself. Rocca expects bitcoin’s next phase of growth to depend on more institutions making long-term allocations. He argues that some participation through exchange-traded funds (ETFs) has involved arbitrage strategies, which differ from a corporate treasurer deciding to allocate a portion of the company’s assets to bitcoin. “People called the institutional cycle too early,” he said. Reduced geopolitical and regulatory uncertainty could help unlock those allocations, potentially pushing bitcoin to $250,000 over the next two to three years, in his view. Xapo’s customers are less united about the immediate outlook. Some are buying because they believe the market has bottomed out; others are keeping their savings in dollars because they expect further declines, while earning interest in bitcoin. For Rocca, that mix still points toward accumulation and demand for banking services that help holders build their positions over several years. coreStoryFacts.text: Wealthy bitcoin $BTC $84,459.46 holders are increasingly treating their cryptocurrency as an asset to borrow against and generate income from, marking a shift from speculation toward private banking, according to Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca.
Xapo currently advertises a variable base rate of 4.1% on dollar savings, paid in bitcoin, alongside a temporary 4.6% introductory rate for eligible new members.
The bank charges an annual membership fee of $1,000, combining dollar banking with access to bitcoin custody, investments and borrowing.
Xapo grew out of a bitcoin custody business known for its Swiss bunker storage.
The crypto banking landscape is entering a new phase.

On October 24, 2026, Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca told CoinDesk that wealthy bitcoin holders are increasingly seeking loans and yield, treating their cryptocurrency as a collateral asset rather than a speculative instrument ( Cryptonews.net ).

That shift from trading mentality to private‑banking‑style wealth preservation carries immediate consequences for Web3 startups and DAOs that hold bitcoin on their balance sheets, and for the platforms that serve them.

A Web3 startup that raised funds in stablecoins and wants to allocate a portion to bitcoin, or a DAO whose treasury holds ETH and BTC, must now answer the same question the wealthy individual does: how do we extract working capital without undermining our long‑position?
The gap between what wealthy holders can do at a private bank and what a DAO can do with its own treasury is exactly where the next generation of crypto‑banking must deliver.
Bitcoin is being reclassified – from a speculative asset to the foundation of a private‑banking relationship.
Xapo, which began as a custody service, now charges a $1,000 annual membership for a bundle that includes dollar banking, bitcoin custody, investments, and borrowing.
The bank’s clients want the tools previously reserved for traditional wealth management, only anchored to their crypto holdings.
This infrastructure does not provide loans or yield itself; it is the rails that make those strategies executable.
That is the fiat‑crypto integration that wealthy individuals demand from their private bank, packaged for the Web3 business.

Beyond plain bitcoin loans, watch for on‑chain credit markets that use reputation and cash‑flow history, tokenized private credit, and yield‑bearing stablecoins that pay interest directly in the wallet.

For a DAO that already manages its treasury through a platform like OneSafe, adding a yield component may be as simple as allocating a percentage of USDC to a regulated yield protocol and then settling gains back into the fiat account automatically.

However, tapping into yield or borrowing requires an operational layer that securely holds your crypto, connects to lending protocols or banks without manual sweeps, and keeps fiat‑crypto flows transparent for accounting and compliance.
Whether or not your business pursues loans, the market expectation is now that a modern treasury can seamlessly convert crypto to working capital when needed.
For years, companies juggled a traditional bank account for fiat and a separate crypto exchange or custodian.
Only after this operational layer is solid should you explore lending partnerships, so that bitcoin‑backed loans flow directly into a governed fiat account without bottlenecks.
OneSafe brings together your crypto and banking needs in one simple, powerful platform.
Standard Chartered may merge Zodia Custody into its banking division, reshaping crypto banking for businesses and DAOs.

Today, a small but growing group of platforms offers neo‑banking for startups – real multi‑currency accounts, ACH and wire transfers, corporate cards, invoicing, and integrated crypto‑to‑fiat conversions.
Visa’s analysis of crypto in banking confirms that embedded crypto capabilities are rapidly becoming a customer expectation.

At the Gibraltar-based bank, customers are seeking cash without selling their bitcoin, putting some of their holdings into income-generating investments, or accumulating more $BTC through interest paid on dollar savings, he said. “Customers are looking for yield and alpha,” Rocca told CoinDesk in an interview, pointing to demand from funds and family offices for accumulation and income products. The behavior reflects bitcoin’s growing maturity, he said. Five or six years ago, the cryptocurrency was primarily viewed as a trading and speculative asset. Today, more holders want financial services built around their existing wealth. Xapo grew out of a bitcoin custody business known for its Swiss bunker storage. Its customers include early adopters who have experienced several halvings (the periodic reductions in new bitcoin issuance), and the rallies and downturns surrounding them. The bank charges an annual membership fee of $1,000, combining dollar banking with access to bitcoin custody, investments and borrowing. Experience has pushed those customers in different directions. Some of the earliest adopters became more willing to take profits as bitcoin reached record prices, having watched gains disappear in previous downturns, Rocca said. Others, including investors who entered around 2018 and 2019, remain determined to hold and prefer borrowing against their coins when they need liquidity. For the profit-takers, selling does not necessarily mean abandoning bitcoin. Some keep the proceeds in dollar savings accounts and receive interest in $BTC , gradually rebuilding their cryptocurrency holdings while retaining cash. Rocca said about 45% of Xapo customers use that feature. Xapo currently advertises a variable base rate of 4.1% on dollar savings, paid in bitcoin, alongside a temporary 4.6% introductory rate for eligible new members. It’s a separate bitcoin credit fund that targets annual returns of up to 4% through lending, exposing investors to credit and counterparty risk. The common thread is the demand to make existing wealth productive. “The theme of this cycle is yield, accumulation, income generation,” Rocca said. Borrowing allows customers to retain exposure to future bitcoin gains, although they also remain exposed to price declines while taking on debt. Traditional banks increasingly acknowledge that clients want bitcoin exposure, Rocca said. Their interest in custody and investment products represents a substantial change from the skepticism he encountered when he began working in crypto in 2016.

relevantPassages.text: The crypto banking landscape is entering a new phase.

On October 24, 2026, Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca told CoinDesk that wealthy bitcoin holders are increasingly seeking loans and yield, treating their cryptocurrency as a collateral asset rather than a speculative instrument ( Cryptonews.net ).

That shift from trading mentality to private‑banking‑style wealth preservation carries immediate consequences for Web3 startups and DAOs that hold bitcoin on their balance sheets, and for the platforms that serve them.

A Web3 startup that raised funds in stablecoins and wants to allocate a portion to bitcoin, or a DAO whose treasury holds ETH and BTC, must now answer the same question the wealthy individual does: how do we extract working capital without undermining our long‑position?
The gap between what wealthy holders can do at a private bank and what a DAO can do with its own treasury is exactly where the next generation of crypto‑banking must deliver.
Bitcoin is being reclassified – from a speculative asset to the foundation of a private‑banking relationship.
Xapo, which began as a custody service, now charges a $1,000 annual membership for a bundle that includes dollar banking, bitcoin custody, investments, and borrowing.
The bank’s clients want the tools previously reserved for traditional wealth management, only anchored to their crypto holdings.
This infrastructure does not provide loans or yield itself; it is the rails that make those strategies executable.
That is the fiat‑crypto integration that wealthy individuals demand from their private bank, packaged for the Web3 business.

Beyond plain bitcoin loans, watch for on‑chain credit markets that use reputation and cash‑flow history, tokenized private credit, and yield‑bearing stablecoins that pay interest directly in the wallet.

For a DAO that already manages its treasury through a platform like OneSafe, adding a yield component may be as simple as allocating a percentage of USDC to a regulated yield protocol and then settling gains back into the fiat account automatically.

However, tapping into yield or borrowing requires an operational layer that securely holds your crypto, connects to lending protocols or banks without manual sweeps, and keeps fiat‑crypto flows transparent for accounting and compliance.
Whether or not your business pursues loans, the market expectation is now that a modern treasury can seamlessly convert crypto to working capital when needed.
For years, companies juggled a traditional bank account for fiat and a separate crypto exchange or custodian.
Only after this operational layer is solid should you explore lending partnerships, so that bitcoin‑backed loans flow directly into a governed fiat account without bottlenecks.
OneSafe brings together your crypto and banking needs in one simple, powerful platform.
Standard Chartered may merge Zodia Custody into its banking division, reshaping crypto banking for businesses and DAOs.

Today, a small but growing group of platforms offers neo‑banking for startups – real multi‑currency accounts, ACH and wire transfers, corporate cards, invoicing, and integrated crypto‑to‑fiat conversions.
Visa’s analysis of crypto in banking confirms that embedded crypto capabilities are rapidly becoming a customer expectation.
As the line between crypto and traditional banking blurs, businesses that have already unified their fiat‑crypto operations will be best positioned to adopt new products without retrofitting.

extraction.body: Wealthy bitcoin BTC $84,459.46 holders are increasingly treating their cryptocurrency as an asset to borrow against and generate income from, marking a shift from speculation toward private banking, according to Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca. At the Gibraltar-based bank, customers are seeking cash without selling their bitcoin, putting some of their holdings into income-generating investments, or accumulating more BTC through interest paid on dollar savings, he said. “Customers are looking for yield and alpha,” Rocca told CoinDesk in an interview, pointing to demand from funds and family offices for accumulation and income products. The behavior reflects bitcoin’s growing maturity, he said. Five or six years ago, the cryptocurrency was primarily viewed as a trading and speculative asset. Today, more holders want financial services built around their existing wealth. Xapo grew out of a bitcoin custody business known for its Swiss bunker storage. Its customers include early adopters who have experienced several halvings (the periodic reductions in new bitcoin issuance), and the rallies and downturns surrounding them. The bank charges an annual membership fee of $1,000, combining dollar banking with access to bitcoin custody, investments and borrowing. Experience has pushed those customers in different directions. Some of the earliest adopters became more willing to take profits as bitcoin reached record prices, having watched gains disappear in previous downturns, Rocca said. Others, including investors who entered around 2018 and 2019, remain determined to hold and prefer borrowing against their coins when they need liquidity. For the profit-takers, selling does not necessarily mean abandoning bitcoin. Some keep the proceeds in dollar savings accounts and receive interest in BTC, gradually rebuilding their cryptocurrency holdings while retaining cash. Rocca said about 45% of Xapo customers use that feature. Xapo currently advertises a variable base rate of 4.1% on dollar savings, paid in bitcoin, alongside a temporary 4.6% introductory rate for eligible new members. It’s a separate bitcoin credit fund that targets annual returns of up to 4% through lending, exposing investors to credit and counterparty risk. The common thread is the demand to make existing wealth productive. “The theme of this cycle is yield, accumulation, income generation,” Rocca said. Borrowing allows customers to retain exposure to future bitcoin gains, although they also remain exposed to price declines while taking on debt. Traditional banks increasingly acknowledge that clients want bitcoin exposure, Rocca said. Their interest in custody and investment products represents a substantial change from the skepticism he encountered when he began working in crypto in 2016. “Big banks are slow,” he said, describing institutions where new products require committee approvals and employees are reluctant to champion activities perceived as risky. Political and regulatory uncertainty adds to that caution. Banks that previously feared repercussions from serving crypto businesses need confidence that a more accommodating environment will endure before committing resources, he said. For now, some institutions are doing enough to meet customer demand through investment products, while stopping short of services that let clients borrow against or directly manage bitcoin wealth. “Them being slow is a good opportunity for firms like Xapo Bank,” Rocca said. He also sees benefits in a measured approach, arguing that another failure involving poorly managed crypto businesses could damage confidence in bitcoin itself. Rocca expects bitcoin’s next phase of growth to depend on more institutions making long-term allocations. He argues that some participation through exchange-traded funds (ETFs) has involved arbitrage strategies, which differ from a corporate treasurer deciding to allocate a portion of the company’s assets to bitcoin. “People called the institutional cycle too early,” he said. Reduced geopolitical and regulatory uncertainty could help unlock those allocations, potentially pushing bitcoin to $250,000 over the next two to three years, in his view. Xapo’s customers are less united about the immediate outlook. Some are buying because they believe the market has bottomed out; others are keeping their savings in dollars because they expect further declines, while earning interest in bitcoin. For Rocca, that mix still points toward accumulation and demand for banking services that help holders build their positions over several years. passages: The CNET data makes one thing clear for Apple: a folding iPhone doesn’t need universal appeal to be a major success.
Capturing even a committed slice of its user base would be enough to drive record-breaking upgrade cycles and open a powerful new revenue stream. ‎ MacDailyNews Take: The math is compelling.
Apple currently has approximately 1.6 billion active iPhones worldwide.

If iPhone owners mirror the overall U.S. smartphone population’s interest in foldables — a reasonable assumption given Apple’s track record of popularizing premium features — that 14% equates to roughly 224 million potential folding iPhone sales.
Of course, not every interested owner will upgrade right away.
Pricing, reliability, trade-in offers, and carrier promotions will all influence actual conversion rates.
To put that number in context: Apple shipped a record 247 million iPhones in 2025.
A folding model that successfully captured the interest of just 14% of existing owners could nearly match an entire year’s current shipment volume — all from upgrades within Apple’s own ecosystem.
Now, that you’ve read our report and Take, please go to CNET and read how differently they approach the numbers they found here .
Keep in mind that CNET never mentions just how many iPhone users are represented by 14%.
But how many said they were interested/would consider upgrading if it started at $1,999?!
And once it’s in-hand, the feel how thick it is, how costly it is, what’s the benefit over a dedicated iPad Mini or MacBook model they have and a traditionally designed iPhone?
In fact, the first foldable iPhone is expected to be unveiled this year.
Samsung has sold tens of millions of foldables over the past several years, yet they still make up only a small percentage of total smartphone sales.
Apple is already evaluating next-generation prototypes of its foldable iPhone Duo that incorporate under-display Face ID on the outer screen…
Apple on Thursday released iOS 27.1, a software update available exclusively to owners of the iPhone Duo.

extraction.body: Apple's first foldable has new screen dimensions, leaving apps with a lot of unused space or awkward cropping. It'll get better over time. For some lucky Apple superfans , today is the day they get to unbox their iPhone Duo . (Others may have to wait until January .) But after formally transferring all their software, they’ll discover a troubling truth: Some of their favorite apps look bad, with awkwardly unused space. Yet the message from CNET phone reviewers over the decades is reassuring. If precedent is anything to go by, updates will be coming to adjust apps to the iPhone Duo’s novel screen ratios, from the squat and wide front screen to the 4:3 inner display. Don’t worry — your apps will get better (and some are already tuned to the device’s dimensions ). That may be little comfort for Duo owners looking forlornly at Android foldables, which have had the better part of a decade on the market for app makers to adjust to the new formats. Despite having a similar passport-sized format to Apple’s foldable, most apps are sized correctly for the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 . But that wasn’t the case with the first Samsung Galaxy Fold , which launched in early 2019, as CNET Editor at Large Andy Lanxon recalls. “I had exactly the same experience when I used the first Samsung Galaxy Fold on the day it came out, with many apps appearing to be oddly squashed into that larger inner display,” Lanxon said. “Over time, both Android and foldable makers like Samsung and Google developed better software to accommodate foldables, and I’m confident that Apple won’t take long to patch up any shortcomings in this area.” Indeed, it’s easy to forget that as the world’s first mainstream foldable, the original Galaxy Fold launched with plenty of display, hinge and other hardware problems that were ironed out over the years. Apple’s first foldable benefits from that refinement, launching with a minimal crease, a smooth and seemingly durable hinge, internal software suited to a folding screen (with FOMO-inspiring animations ), IP68 dust- and water-resistance and other qualities that ease use. The Duo also benefits from being a single design, as opposed to the various screen sizes and formats across all the Android foldables. The Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra , for instance, both have 6.5-inch outer screens and 8-inch inner screens, but the former is slightly wider yet shorter than the latter. But it’s the Duo’s specific design that might also accelerate app adjustment, Lanxon notes: The outer display has the same aspect ratio as the larger inner display, something Apple highlighted during its Sept. 9 presentation launching the device. So developers only need to design one app size for the Duo that will work perfectly well on both displays. Compare that to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, which pairs a tall and narrow 21:9 cover screen with an almost square 10:9 inner screen. That’s somewhat reassuring, but what iPhone Duo owners likely want to know is: When will my apps get updated? To predict that, we look to the past — both the development of other foldables and the radical changes in Apple’s own iPhone line . The iPhone X, revealed on stage in October 2017, shifted to an all-glass front panel and the notorious notch at the top, requiring apps to adjust. Given how long smartphones have had all-glass front panels, it’s understandable that it takes time to adapt apps to foldable displays. But it’s easy to forget that app makers had to go through the same process before when phones finally ditched physical buttons below screens for the all-glass front to begin with. “I remember when the iPhone X came out, and apps that hadn’t been optimized had black bars above and below,” said CNET Editor at Large Scott Stein, who reviewed the device back in 2017. “It meant all apps didn’t initially make the most of the new phone’s size.” The Duo will have the same growing pains until more apps get optimized, Stein added — it takes time, and it’s part of what it means to be a hardware early adopter. The original Samsung Galaxy Fold, launched in Feb. 2019. It’s important to remember how complex it is to make software for a foldable, as explained by Jessica Dolcourt, CNET Group and CNET Labs vice president of content operations and commerce. When you open and close a foldable device, you’re asking your app to perform acrobatics, instantly leaping between internal and external displays while simultaneously expanding or contracting the view window and rearranging all the pixels. Dolcourt spent over a decade reviewing phones for CNET, including the original Samsung Galaxy Fold in 2019, where she got her first taste of apps rendering badly. “Native apps could be slow to load, but brought the vision of a foldable future to life. Third-party apps — which were most of them — struggled to catch up quickly and smoothly to the demands of a folding screen,” Dolcourt said. “At the outset, some were barely usable.” Nowadays, most apps are designed for Android foldables, in part thanks to years of Google software updates specifically addressing flexible displays. The Duo will have to play catch-up. But as Lanxon pointed out, Apple has deep relationships with developers of its apps, which sometimes launch on iOS first before heading to the Google Play Store. Apple will surely be working closely with its software partners to ensure they’re using the Duo’s proportions to the best advantage, Lanxon said. When your apps, like Instagram, will be updated to fit the Duo’s screens is hard to gauge (especially given it took 15 years to get an iPad-native Instagram app ), but developers have many more advantages than they did when adapting to the first Android foldables’ displays. Over time — and hopefully soon — the Duo will be even better to use as apps catch up with it. © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

extraction.body: Apple's first foldable has new screen dimensions, leaving apps with a lot of unused space or awkward cropping. It'll get better over time. For some lucky Apple superfans , today is the day they get to unbox their iPhone Duo . (Others may have to wait until January .) But after formally transferring all their software, they’ll discover a troubling truth: Some of their favorite apps look bad, with awkwardly unused space. Yet the message from CNET phone reviewers over the decades is reassuring. If precedent is anything to go by, updates will be coming to adjust apps to the iPhone Duo’s novel screen ratios, from the squat and wide front screen to the 4:3 inner display. Don’t worry — your apps will get better (and some are already tuned to the device’s dimensions ). That may be little comfort for Duo owners looking forlornly at Android foldables, which have had the better part of a decade on the market for app makers to adjust to the new formats. Despite having a similar passport-sized format to Apple’s foldable, most apps are sized correctly for the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 . But that wasn’t the case with the first Samsung Galaxy Fold , which launched in early 2019, as CNET Editor at Large Andy Lanxon recalls. “I had exactly the same experience when I used the first Samsung Galaxy Fold on the day it came out, with many apps appearing to be oddly squashed into that larger inner display,” Lanxon said. “Over time, both Android and foldable makers like Samsung and Google developed better software to accommodate foldables, and I’m confident that Apple won’t take long to patch up any shortcomings in this area.” Indeed, it’s easy to forget that as the world’s first mainstream foldable, the original Galaxy Fold launched with plenty of display, hinge and other hardware problems that were ironed out over the years. Apple’s first foldable benefits from that refinement, launching with a minimal crease, a smooth and seemingly durable hinge, internal software suited to a folding screen (with FOMO-inspiring animations ), IP68 dust- and water-resistance and other qualities that ease use. The Duo also benefits from being a single design, as opposed to the various screen sizes and formats across all the Android foldables. The Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra , for instance, both have 6.5-inch outer screens and 8-inch inner screens, but the former is slightly wider yet shorter than the latter. But it’s the Duo’s specific design that might also accelerate app adjustment, Lanxon notes: The outer display has the same aspect ratio as the larger inner display, something Apple highlighted during its Sept. 9 presentation launching the device. So developers only need to design one app size for the Duo that will work perfectly well on both displays. Compare that to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, which pairs a tall and narrow 21:9 cover screen with an almost square 10:9 inner screen. That’s somewhat reassuring, but what iPhone Duo owners likely want to know is: When will my apps get updated? To predict that, we look to the past — both the development of other foldables and the radical changes in Apple’s own iPhone line . The iPhone X, revealed on stage in October 2017, shifted to an all-glass front panel and the notorious notch at the top, requiring apps to adjust. Given how long smartphones have had all-glass front panels, it’s understandable that it takes time to adapt apps to foldable displays. But it’s easy to forget that app makers had to go through the same process before when phones finally ditched physical buttons below screens for the all-glass front to begin with. “I remember when the iPhone X came out, and apps that hadn’t been optimized had black bars above and below,” said CNET Editor at Large Scott Stein, who reviewed the device back in 2017. “It meant all apps didn’t initially make the most of the new phone’s size.” The Duo will have the same growing pains until more apps get optimized, Stein added — it takes time, and it’s part of what it means to be a hardware early adopter. The original Samsung Galaxy Fold, launched in Feb. 2019. It’s important to remember how complex it is to make software for a foldable, as explained by Jessica Dolcourt, CNET Group and CNET Labs vice president of content operations and commerce. When you open and close a foldable device, you’re asking your app to perform acrobatics, instantly leaping between internal and external displays while simultaneously expanding or contracting the view window and rearranging all the pixels. Dolcourt spent over a decade reviewing phones for CNET, including the original Samsung Galaxy Fold in 2019, where she got her first taste of apps rendering badly. “Native apps could be slow to load, but brought the vision of a foldable future to life. Third-party apps — which were most of them — struggled to catch up quickly and smoothly to the demands of a folding screen,” Dolcourt said. “At the outset, some were barely usable.” Nowadays, most apps are designed for Android foldables, in part thanks to years of Google software updates specifically addressing flexible displays. The Duo will have to play catch-up. But as Lanxon pointed out, Apple has deep relationships with developers of its apps, which sometimes launch on iOS first before heading to the Google Play Store. Apple will surely be working closely with its software partners to ensure they’re using the Duo’s proportions to the best advantage, Lanxon said. When your apps, like Instagram, will be updated to fit the Duo’s screens is hard to gauge (especially given it took 15 years to get an iPad-native Instagram app ), but developers have many more advantages than they did when adapting to the first Android foldables’ displays. Over time — and hopefully soon — the Duo will be even better to use as apps catch up with it. © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

12,751,749, titled “System for Joint Fixation of Extremity Bone and Related Methods.” The patent, which issued October 6, 2026, covers surgical methods for what Forma calls minimally invasive plate arthrodesis, or MIPA™, in which a plate is introduced and secured across a joint of the foot through small incisions rather than a traditional open exposure.
By combining stable plate fixation with smaller incisions, MIPA addresses a critical trade-off, potentially driving broader adoption.
This approach aims to meet both surgeon preference for robust fixation and patient demand for less invasive procedures, enhancing market competitiveness.
“The fixation surgeons trust, through the small incisions patients ask for.
That is what surgeons told us they needed, and MIPA is designed to deliver both,” said Andrew C.
“This patent covers the method, not a single implant.

extraction.body: CAMP HILL, Pa.--( BUSINESS WIRE )--Forma Medical Inc. announced today that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office has issued U.S. Patent No. 12,751,749, titled “System for Joint Fixation of Extremity Bone and Related Methods.” The patent, which issued October 6, 2026, covers surgical methods for what Forma calls minimally invasive plate arthrodesis, or MIPA™, in which a plate is introduced and secured across a joint of the foot through small incisions rather than a traditional open exposure. Fusion surgery, or arthrodesis, permanently joins two bones across a joint damaged by arthritis or deformity. It is a mainstay of foot and ankle reconstruction at the big toe, the midfoot, and the hindfoot. Surgeons have long faced a trade-off in how they perform it. Plates provide stable, well-established fixation but have traditionally required a longer incision to implant. Minimally invasive techniques shrink the incision but have typically relied on a screw-only construct. MIPA is designed to remove that trade-off. The name echoes a shift in fracture care. Since the 1990s, orthopedic trauma surgeons have adopted minimally invasive plate osteosynthesis (MIPO), sliding fracture plates beneath the skin through small incisions to protect the surrounding soft tissue and blood supply. MIPA applies the same principles to joint fusion. “The fixation surgeons trust, through the small incisions patients ask for. That is what surgeons told us they needed, and MIPA is designed to deliver both,” said Andrew C. Davison, CEO of Forma Medical. “This patent covers the method, not a single implant. The big toe was our starting point, with more than 1,000 procedures to date. The claims extend to other joints of the foot where surgeons already reach for a plate.” “In urgent fracture care, we have evolved to less invasive surgical approaches for internal fixation, with less anatomic distortion and soft tissue dissection,” said Jesse F. Doty, MD, FAAOS, a fellowship-trained orthopedic foot and ankle surgeon at Integrity Orthopedics and Professor of Orthopaedic Surgery at the University of Tennessee and a co-inventor of the patented technology. “Elective fusion has been slower to progress to an established equivalent until now. MIPA offers a defined, repeatable way to deliver more robust plate fixation through smaller incisions, providing the same benefits we've seen from minimally invasive surgery in other anatomic areas, but without compromised stability. I’ve used MIPA for MTP joint fusions in my own practice for years now. My experience and patient feedback have been highly encouraging, and I plan to submit my clinical outcomes for publication later this year.” About Forma Medical Forma Medical Inc. is a privately held orthopedic device company focused on developing differentiated solutions that combine strong biomechanical principles with minimally invasive surgical techniques. The company’s flagship OptimalMTP® system is designed to advance the standard of care in first MTP joint fusion by delivering stability, reproducibility, and efficiency through an MIS approach. OptimalMTP received FDA 510(k) clearance in 2024 and has been used in more than 1,000 procedures. James A.
